description: STM32 bare-metal Rust firmware using the Embassy async framework — #[embassy_executor::main], async GPIO blink on PA5, and a DMA-backed async UART echo on USART2/PA2-PA3. Targets STM32F411RE (Nucleo/Black Pill); swap HAL feature + memory.x for other chips. Flash + RTT via probe-rs.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick for STM32F/L/G series firmware in Rust when you want async/await (Embassy). For synchronous cortex-m-rt + RTIC, pick a different starter. For Raspberry Pi Pico, use rp2040-embassy.
firstSteps: Install the Cortex-M4F target: rustup target add thumbv7em-none-eabihf
Install the flasher: cargo install probe-rs --features cli --locked
Connect an ST-Link (or any CMSIS-DAP probe) to the board
Flash + RTT: cargo run --release   (runs `probe-rs run --chip STM32F411RETx` via the cargo runner)
Open a serial terminal at 115200 baud on the Nucleo's USB COM port — anything you type echoes back
gotchas: memory.x must match the actual chip. STM32F411RE = 512K flash + 128K RAM; STM32F401RE = 512K flash + 96K RAM; STM32F103C8 = 64K flash + 20K RAM. Wrong values silently let the linker succeed then crash at boot.
embassy-stm32 requires exactly one chip feature — e.g. `stm32f411re`. Enabling two (or none) is a compile error with a misleading `time_driver_tim5 not found` message.
The cortex-m-rt link args (`-Tlink.x`, `-Tdefmt.x`) must be in .cargo/config.toml rustflags. If you put them in build.rs alone they only apply when the `build.rs` crate links, not the downstream bin.
defmt-rtt requires a running probe-rs to drain the RTT buffer. Without a probe attached at runtime the firmware will spin waiting for the RTT reader after ~1KB of logs.
Changing memory.x requires `cargo clean` — cargo does not see memory.x as a build input so the linker will use a stale copy from target/.

UART echo uses DMA1_CH6 (TX, stream 6) and DMA1_CH5 (RX, stream 5) for USART2. On STM32F4, channel numbers in Embed.toml refer to DMA streams. Swapping to a different UART requires picking the matching DMA stream pair from the STM32F4 reference manual.
bind_interrupts! must name the exact peripheral interrupt (USART2) that matches the peripheral passed to Uart::new. Mismatches are link-time errors, not compile-time.
architectureNotes: Two tasks: the main task owns the LED and blinks at 500 ms; uart_echo_task owns the UART peripheral and echoes bytes. Embassy's executor multiplexes them cooperatively — no RTOS tick required.

Owned peripherals passed into a spawned task satisfy 'static because the peripheral tokens are zero-sized move-only values created by embassy_stm32::init(). The executor stores the task future in static memory.
DMA-backed UART read/write avoids CPU-spin in the echo loop. The DMA transfer completes asynchronously; the task yields via .await until the hardware interrupt fires.

placeholders.description: LED pin is PA5 (Nucleo-F401RE/F411RE). Change to PD12 for STM32F4-Discovery or PC13 (active-low) for Black Pill.
UART is USART2 on PA2 (TX) / PA3 (RX) — the Nucleo VCP bridge. Change peripheral + pins + DMA channels for boards without a VCP or when using a different UART.
chip = STM32F411RETx. Swap to STM32F401RETx for Nucleo-F401RE, STM32F407VGTx for STM32F4-Discovery, STM32F411CEUx for Black Pill.
